findings.source_passage: You have seen Italian organ-boys holding a dancing-ape by a long cord. Just so, from the ship's steep side, did I hold Queequeg down there in the sea
findings.why_it_matters: The Italian organ-boys simile is a distinctive, voice-establishing figure that gives the monkey-rope image its concrete visual character; its absence flattens the narrator's analogical wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the organ-boys simile before introducing the monkey-rope technical term.

findings.source_passage: Queequeg was my own inseparable twin brother; nor could I any way get rid of the dangerous liabilities which the hempen bond entailed.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence clinches the Siamese-twin conceit with the legal/contractual idiom ('liabilities,' 'hempen bond') that Melville will echo in the philosophical paragraph; losing it weakens the rhetorical setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Queequeg was my own inseparable twin brother; nor could I any way get rid of the dangerous liabilities which the hempen bond entailed' after the wedding conceit.

findings.source_passage: "Ginger? Do I smell ginger?" suspiciously asked Stubb… "Ginger? ginger? and will you have the goodness to tell me, Mr. Dough-Boy, where lies the virtue of ginger?"
findings.why_it_matters: The full comic escalation of Stubb's ginger tirade—its rhetorical buildup from suspicious sniff to incredulous catalog—is a signature comic set-piece; the draft collapses it to a single spliced fragment, erasing Melville's carefully staged comedic rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's full first speech at least through 'where lies the virtue of ginger?' before the firewood/gunpowder catalog.

findings.source_passage: "There is some sneaking Temperance Society movement about this business," he suddenly added, now approaching Starbuck… "Will you look at that kannakin, sir: smell of it, if you please."
findings.why_it_matters: The direct-speech texture of Stubb's appeal to Starbuck (sniffing the kannakin, the formal 'smell of it, if you please') contributes to the scene's comic formality; flattening to indirect report loses the register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least one full speech-act of Stubb's address to Starbuck in direct dialogue.

findings.source_passage: "Oh, I never hurt when I hit, except when I hit a whale or something of that sort; and this fellow's a weazel."
findings.source_locator: Stubb's retort to Starbuck, dialogue section
findings.why_it_matters: Stubb's self-characterizing quip ('I never hurt when I hit…') is a small but voice-rich moment that reveals his bluff self-image; it is cut entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's weazel line as part of the dialogue compression.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; the central philosophical paragraph and the allegory passage are faithfully reproduced verbatim, but three medium-severity flattenings (organ-boys simile, twin-brother close, Stubb's full ginger tirade) erode the chapter's comic and rhetorical texture without quite triggering regeneration.
